title: A Local DNS Benchmark Helps Gamers Compare Resolvers

cover.subtitle: Compare local lookup speed and reliability.
cover.visual: A stopwatch beside two resolver cards, with a separate game controller. No speed scores, no winner badge.

sections.name: 01-separate-lookup-time-from-the-game-connection
sections.heading: Lookup time and game latency measure different operations
sections.scene: Two separate rows. Top: laptop asks resolver for a hostname. Bottom: game controller connects to game server. No arrow between resolver and gameplay latency. Only labels DNS lookup and Game connection.
sections.alt: Lookup time and game latency measure different operations.

sections.name: 02-build-a-controlled-comparison-on-one-device
sections.heading: A controlled comparison keeps device conditions consistent
sections.scene: One laptop connects to two side-by-side candidate resolver cards. A worksheet records duration and answer. Equal visual prominence, no winner.
sections.alt: A controlled comparison keeps device conditions consistent.

sections.name: 03-repeat-queries-and-retain-failures-in-the-results
sections.heading: Repeated queries reveal slow answers and failures
sections.scene: A timing worksheet contains rows of dots for repeated trials. One amber timeout marker remains visible beside successful trials. No invented numeric measurements.
sections.alt: Repeated queries reveal slow answers and failures.

sections.name: 04-verify-the-application-and-preserve-an-easy-rollback
sections.heading: Application checks confirm the resolver change works
sections.scene: A settings card has a saved original configuration beside a trial configuration. A curved return arrow links trial to original. A game controller sits separately.
sections.alt: Application checks confirm the resolver change works.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
